rationale: The workflow repeatedly downloads pip dependencies across a large Python-version matrix with no dependency cache. Evidence pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (cache dependency downloads, reported modest aggregate benefit) and the measured fork experiment (pip cache added before dependency install, ~9.2% elapsed savings) support adding a pip cache. Prerequisites are met: requirements.txt and pyproject.toml exist, pip installs are performed, and setup-python is used. The cache key includes runner.os, matrix.python-version, and hashes of requirements.txt/pyproject.toml so caches are not shared across incompatible Python versions or dependency changes; restore-keys only affect hit rate, not resolved versions, so install correctness and test coverage are preserved. No permissions are weakened, and no secrets, publishing/deployment, or new network access is added.
